children: Innok Robotics Group AG began a six-month pilot on 13 November, operating an autonomous robot between its headquarters and a REWE supermarket in Regenstauf. If successful, the operating area may be extended to other districts.
Six-month public-road robot pilot began Nov. 13
The approved real-world deployment tests whether Innok can extend its autonomous logistics business beyond enclosed sites.
Robot currently travels about 1 km to a REWE store
The initial route is limited; broader customer delivery depends on a successful pilot and subsequent expansion.
Expansion to other districts is conditional on success
Direct-to-customer grocery delivery is a stated next step, not an established service or quantified revenue stream.
Pilot enables testing across public roads for industrial sites
The company says public-road permissions had constrained cross-site industrial transport; broader use would require further approvals.

This is an early-stage operational milestone for Innok Robotics, with no revenue impact or financial terms disclosed. A successful pilot, expansion of the operating area, and further permissions for customer or industrial routes would be needed to establish a larger commercial catalyst.
from Innok Robotics Group AG distributed by EQS.
